students.name: Lee: diagnosis with a short-route preference
students.narrative: Lee is fascinated by differential diagnosis and explains case stories from a school health club. Lee currently hopes to start earning quickly and chooses dental assisting preparation, despite preferring physician responsibilities in the role questions. These are two real preferences to discuss rather than proof the routes are interchangeable. Lee wants an expensive future lifestyle before understanding its training timeline.
students.observedContext: Health-club reading and family conversations; no clinical performance experience. The short route reflects current money concerns, not inability to study.
students.unmeasuredLimits: The model is a route-conflict check. Neither an expensive goal nor an education preference is an aptitude score.

students.name: Taylor: outdoor environmental questions
students.narrative: Taylor likes comparing stream measurements, keeping field notes and returning after rain to see what changed. Outdoor evidence and uncertainty are interesting; treating people and managing a shop are not. Taylor is willing to study science and wants a simple lifestyle with room for hiking equipment rather than expensive dining.
students.observedContext: Joined a supervised water-monitoring club and entered results into a shared sheet. Repeated measurements when a reading looked inconsistent.
students.unmeasuredLimits: Club measurements do not establish scientific aptitude or readiness for hazardous fieldwork.

students.name: River: structures under constraints
students.narrative: River likes physics, model bridges and testing a design until it handles a load. Drawing for expression is enjoyable sometimes, but calculations and safety constraints are the main attraction. River wants engineering study, is prepared to revise a weak design, and dreams of owning a modest home after training.
students.observedContext: Built and tested a small model bridge in class and documented its failure points. Has no professional design or construction authority.
students.unmeasuredLimits: Classroom models do not establish engineering aptitude or competence to design public structures.

Texas electrician license for non-exempt work.

students.name: Sky: cooking without management
students.narrative: Sky likes planning the order of cooking tasks, testing a recipe and preparing food safely for others. Owning a restaurant, bargaining and supervising staff are not appealing. Many official activities are unrelated to cooking and receive unsure or dislike responses; the detailed food interest should still be visible as something to explore, not a forced management identity.
students.observedContext: Prepares several family meals each week and helped at a supervised school food event. Adult oversight is still needed for large-service food safety.
students.unmeasuredLimits: Cooking at home is neither a professional aptitude result nor proof that restaurant work, hours or earnings will suit Sky.

students.name: Jordan: calm prepared response
students.narrative: Jordan likes first-aid practice, repeated procedures and helping a team respond calmly. Clinical diagnosis over years is less appealing than trained immediate care. Jordan wants an EMT course or related training, accepts varied hours as something to investigate, and values practical service more than expensive travel.
students.observedContext: Attended an introductory first-aid course and practiced scenarios with an instructor. Has not provided independent emergency care.
students.unmeasuredLimits: Scenario practice does not establish crisis performance, medical competence or fitness for emergency work.
